lessons.title: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren: holiday types and what you feel like doing
lessons.goal: Name holiday types, say what you like and dislike on holiday, and say what you feel like doing with Lust, Zeit, Spaß and Idee + zu + infinitive.

grammar.topic: zu + infinitive after Lust, Zeit, Spaß, Idee
grammar.point: After nouns like Lust, Zeit, Spaß and Idee (with haben or machen) a second part follows after a comma. Its verb is an infinitive and zu stands directly before it, at the very end: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren. After a modal verb there is no zu: Ich möchte ans Meer fahren.
grammar.oneLine: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren.

mistake.wrong: Ich habe Lust, zu ans Meer fahren.
mistake.right: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren.
mistake.why: zu does not come right after the comma. It stands directly before the infinitive, and the infinitive is the very last word.

terms.meaning: the basic verb form with the little word zu in front: zu fahren, zu wandern
the basic form of a verb, as in the dictionary: fahren, wandern
können, müssen, wollen, möchte, dürfen, sollen: they never take zu

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Ich möchte ans Meer fahren' to 'Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren'
cards.body: Summer is coming, and the WG in Berlin wants to plan a holiday. This chapter is called Gute Reise! (Have a good trip!): holidays, plans and reasons. Today you say what you feel like doing. After möchte the second verb just stands at the end. After Lust haben a comma and a little word appear: zu.
steps: You already know: Ich möchte am Strand liegen. A modal verb (möchte, kann, muss) sends the second verb to the end, with no zu.
New today: Ich habe Lust, am Strand zu liegen. After Lust haben you write a comma, and zu stands right before the verb at the very end.
By the end you can: say what you feel like doing (and not doing) on holiday, and name six types of holiday.

examples.de: Ich möchte am Strand liegen.
examples.en: I would like to lie on the beach.
examples.why: You know this already: modal verb, infinitive at the end, no zu.

examples.de: Ich habe Lust, am Strand zu liegen.
examples.en: I feel like lying on the beach.
examples.why: New today: Lust haben + comma + zu before the last verb.

cards.more: English does something similar. After can you say I can swim, with no to. But after I am happy you need to: I am happy to swim. German has the same two groups. The modal group (möchte, kann, muss) works like I can swim: no zu. The Lust group (Lust haben, Zeit haben, Spaß machen) works like I am happy to swim: zu comes in. So you already feel this difference in English. Over the next cards you will learn which German words belong to the zu group, and where zu sits.

cards.title: Six types of holiday
cards.body: A holiday has a type. You know Urlaub; now build more words with it: der Badeurlaub (beach), der Städtetrip (city), der Wanderurlaub (hiking), der Campingurlaub, der Aktivurlaub and die Kreuzfahrt (cruise). To say which one is yours: Ich bin eher der Typ für Städtetrips. And: Das ist nichts für mich.
cards.lead: The WG wants a holiday, but everybody wants something different. On this card you meet the six holiday types and who in the WG likes which one, so you can say what kind of holiday-maker you are.

examples.de: Ben mag den Badeurlaub, denn er liegt gern am Strand.
examples.en: Ben likes the beach holiday because he likes lying on the beach.

examples.de: Anna findet einen Städtetrip toll.
examples.en: Anna thinks a city break is great.

examples.de: Mira macht am liebsten Wanderurlaub in den Bergen.
examples.en: Mira likes hiking holidays in the mountains best.

deeper.text: German builds holiday words like Lego: Bade + Urlaub, Wander + Urlaub, Camping + Urlaub. The last part decides the gender, so every -urlaub word is der. Notice too: Urlaub is holiday from a job. Students and school children have die Ferien, not Urlaub. Mira and Leon study, so they say Semesterferien for their break, but Herr Ali has Urlaub.

example.de: Herr Ali hat im August drei Wochen Urlaub.
example.en: Herr Ali has three weeks of holiday in August.

cards.more: Think of ordering pizza. You do not describe every ingredient, you pick a type: Margherita, Salami, Funghi. A holiday works the same way, and the name tells you what is on it. Bade means swim, Wander means hike, Städte means cities. So if you see a new word with Urlaub at the end, you can already guess it is a holiday and the first part says what you do. Practise the chunk: Ich bin eher der Typ für …

cards.title: Lust haben + zu + infinitive
cards.body: Lust haben means to feel like doing something. The thing you feel like doing is a second part after a comma. It has its own verb in the infinitive, and zu stands right before that verb, at the very end. keine Lust haben says you do not feel like it. Hast du Lust, …? is a friendly invitation.
cards.lead: You know the types now. Next you say what you feel like doing in them. This card gives you the four steps of the sentence Ich habe Lust, … zu …, and the question to invite someone.

examples.de: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren.
examples.en: I feel like going to the sea.

examples.de: Hast du Lust, mit uns zu wandern?
examples.en: Do you feel like hiking with us?

examples.de: Leon hat keine Lust, den ganzen Tag am Strand zu liegen.
examples.en: Leon does not feel like lying on the beach all day.

deeper.text: Lust can also be followed by auf and a thing, with no zu: Hast du Lust auf einen Kaffee? Use zu only when you name an action. So ask yourself one question: is there a verb after Lust? If yes, comma and zu. If it is only a noun, use auf and the noun, with no comma.

example.de: Hast du Lust auf einen Kaffee?
example.en: Do you feel like a coffee?

cards.more: Build the sentence like a sandwich. First slice of bread: Ich habe Lust. Then a comma, like a little knife that cuts the sandwich in two. Then the filling: everything else you want to say, like ans Meer. Last slice of bread: zu fahren. The verb always goes in the last slice, and zu sits right in front of it. If you forget the order, say it slowly: who feels like it, comma, what, then zu plus verb.
steps: 1. Main clause with Lust haben: Ich habe Lust
2. Comma: ,
3. The rest of the information: ans Meer
4. zu + infinitive at the very end: zu fahren

cards.title: Zeit, Spaß, Idee: more nouns with zu
cards.body: Lust is not the only noun that opens a zu-part. Zeit haben, Spaß machen and die Idee haben do the same. With Spaß the sentence starts with es, and the person who has the fun is in the dative: Es macht mir Spaß, … zu … . The zu-part always comes after the comma, with the verb last.
cards.lead: Lust is only the first noun of this kind. Here you add three more everyday ones, so you can talk about time, fun and ideas for the holiday in the same pattern.

examples.de: Wir haben keine Zeit, lange zu planen.
examples.en: We do not have time to plan for long.

examples.de: Es macht mir Spaß, neue Städte zu sehen.
examples.en: It is fun for me to see new cities.

examples.de: Anna hat die Idee, nach Lissabon zu fliegen.
examples.en: Anna has the idea of flying to Lisbon.

deeper.text: To say something is not fun, use kein, as with any noun: keinen Spaß, because der Spaß is masculine. Do not put nicht in front of Spaß. The same works for keine Lust and keine Zeit, both feminine. So the whole group follows one rule: a noun says no with kein, and kein takes the ending the noun needs.

example.de: Es macht mir keinen Spaß, bei Regen zu wandern.
example.en: It is no fun for me to hike in the rain.

cards.more: Imagine four little doors in a hallway. Each door has a noun on it: Lust, Zeit, Spaß, Idee. Behind every door is the same room, a zu-part with the verb at the end. You can knock on any door with haben or machen, and you always come into the same room. Es macht mir Spaß has the extra word es at the front, like a doorbell that the sentence needs, but behind the door nothing changes: comma, rest, zu, verb.

rows: Es macht mir Spaß, zu reisen.
Anna hat die Idee, zu fliegen.

cards.title: The comma, and why modals have no zu
cards.body: A modal verb (will, möchte, kann, muss) needs no zu and no comma: Ich will wandern. After Lust, Zeit, Spaß and Idee you need zu. If the zu-part has more than one extra word, always write the comma. If it is only zu + verb, the comma is optional.
cards.lead: You can now build zu-parts. This card puts them next to the modal sentences you already know, so you never mix the two up, and it shows you when the comma is a must.

examples.de: Ben will am Strand liegen.
examples.en: Ben wants to lie on the beach.

examples.de: Ben hat Lust, am Strand zu liegen.
examples.en: Ben feels like lying on the beach.

examples.de: Wir haben Zeit, im Juli zu fahren.
examples.en: We have time to travel in July.

deeper.text: Very short zu-parts are the exception: when only zu and the verb follow, many writers drop the comma, and both ways are correct. Hast du Lust zu kommen? looks fine. But as soon as other words stand in front of zu, the comma helps the reader see where the part starts. Keep the safe habit: always write the comma.

example.de: Hast du Lust zu kommen?
example.en: Do you feel like coming?

cards.more: Think of two kinds of recipes. A modal recipe is short: modal verb, ingredients, verb at the end. No extras. The Lust recipe has one extra step, a comma and zu. A good test for a mistake: if the first verb is can, want, must or would like, there is no zu. Wrong: Ich möchte ans Meer zu fahren. Right: Ich möchte ans Meer fahren. If the first part is Lust haben or Zeit haben, zu is a must.

rows: Ich habe Lust, in den Bergen zu wandern.

cards.title: A mini survey: Lust and Spaß
cards.body: Now use both patterns to say what you like and do not like on holiday. The WG did a mini survey. For simple likes the old frames still work: Ich mag …, … gefällt mir, am liebsten …. For actions use Ich habe (keine) Lust, … zu … or Es macht mir (keinen) Spaß, … zu ….
cards.lead: You have two patterns for actions now: Lust and Spaß. On this card they work together in a small survey, so you can tell the WG what you want and what you do not want.

examples.de: Ben hat Lust, den ganzen Tag zu schwimmen.
examples.en: Ben feels like swimming all day.

examples.de: Mira hat keine Lust, in der Stadt zu bleiben.
examples.en: Mira does not feel like staying in the city.

examples.de: Es macht Leon Spaß, Kajak zu fahren.
examples.en: Leon enjoys kayaking.

deeper.text: Ich habe keine Lust is very direct. Among friends it is fine, but a softer way to say no is Das ist nichts für mich (that is not for me), or Ich bin eher der Typ für … (I am more the type for …). Natives use these chunks all the time. You can learn them as whole pieces.

example.de: Ein Städtetrip ist nichts für mich.
example.en: A city break is not for me.

cards.more: A survey is like a vote with a sentence frame. Instead of a cross on paper, everyone says one sentence with the same frame. Ben: Ich habe Lust, … Anna: Es macht mir Spaß, … Mira: Ich habe Lust, … Leon: Ich habe keine Lust, … Four voices, two frames, and the verb is always last. When you listen to a German group plan a holiday, you will hear these frames again and again. Copy them: they are your toolbox.

rows: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren.
Es macht mir Spaß, in Museen zu gehen.
Ich habe Lust, auf einen hohen Berg zu klettern.
Ich habe keine Lust, nur Museen zu besuchen.

cards.title: In the WG kitchen: Wann fahren wir?
cards.body: Now all four of them talk. Ben wants the sea, Mira wants the mountains, Anna has an idea, and Leon asks the practical question. Read the eight lines and look for zu at the end of every long sentence. Look also at the sentence with möchte: it has no zu.
cards.lead: This is the last card of the lesson. The WG uses everything together in one kitchen talk, like a real conversation you could have in a shared flat.

examples.de: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren.
examples.en: I feel like going to the sea.

examples.de: Es macht mir mehr Spaß, in den Bergen zu wandern.
examples.en: It is more fun for me to hike in the mountains.

examples.de: Habt ihr Zeit, im Juli zwei Wochen zu fahren?
examples.en: Do you have time to go for two weeks in July?

deeper.text: When someone leaves for a trip, you say Gute Reise! It is a short form of Ich wünsche dir eine gute Reise, so the noun is in the accusative. With a masculine noun you can hear it: Guten Flug! Guten Appetit! With feminine or neuter nouns the form looks the same: Gute Fahrt! Schönes Wochenende! The answer is simply Danke, gleichfalls!

example.de: Gute Reise! Viel Spaß in den Bergen!
example.en: Have a good trip! Have fun in the mountains!

cards.more: Read a dialogue like a film scene. First watch only the big picture: who wants what? Ben wants sea, Mira wants mountains, Anna wants Lisbon, Leon wants action. Then read again, and only look at the second part of each long sentence: where is zu? It is right in front of the last word. Then find the one sentence with möchte. It has no zu and no comma. After that, say the lines aloud, switching roles.

rows: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren. Am Strand liegen, schwimmen – das ist Urlaub!
Ich nicht. Es macht mir mehr Spaß, in den Bergen zu wandern.
Ich habe die Idee, nach Lissabon zu fliegen. Dort gibt es Meer und Museen.
Ich habe keine Lust, nur am Strand zu liegen. Ich möchte klettern und Kajak fahren.
Habt ihr Zeit, im Juli zwei Wochen zu fahren?
Ich habe Zeit. Aber ich habe nicht viel Geld.
Dann sind Berge und ein Zelt gut. Das ist billig!

drills.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren.
Ich habe Lust, zu ans Meer fahren.
Ich habe Lust, ans Meer fahren zu.
drills.hint: Where does zu stand: before the last verb or somewhere else?
drills.explanation: zu stands directly before the infinitive at the very end: Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren.

drills.prompt: Write in German: Do you feel like swimming?
drills.hint: Start with the verb haben; then du, Lust, and zu right before swimming.
drills.explanation: Hast du Lust, zu schwimmen?

drills.prompt: Build: Anna has the idea of flying to Lisbon.
drills.hint: Main clause, comma, rest of the information, then zu + verb last.
drills.explanation: Anna hat die Idee, nach Lissabon zu fliegen.

drills.prompt: Es macht mir ___ Spaß, bei Regen zu wandern. (It is no fun.)
drills.hint: Spaß is masculine (der Spaß). Which form of kein goes with it?
drills.explanation: keinen Spaß: kein + masculine object form.

drills.prompt: Mira will in den Bergen wandern. Now with Lust: Mira hat Lust, ___
drills.hint: Keep the same words, add one small word before the verb.
drills.explanation: Mira hat Lust, in den Bergen zu wandern.

drills.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Wir wollen im Juli zu fahren.
Wir haben Lust, im Juli fahren.
drills.hint: wollen is a modal verb. Does a modal verb take zu?
drills.explanation: After a modal verb there is no zu: Wir wollen im Juli fahren.

blind.prompt: Write in German: It is fun for Leon to climb in the mountains.
answers: Es macht Leon Spaß, in den Bergen zu klettern.
blind.hint: Start with es, then macht, the person (dative) and Spaß; then the zu-part.
blind.explanation: Es macht Leon Spaß, in den Bergen zu klettern.

check.prompt: Anna hat die Idee, nach Lissabon ___.
check.hint: Where does zu go, and which form of the verb follows?
check.explanation: zu + infinitive: nach Lissabon zu fliegen.

check.prompt: Which holiday is a trip to a city to see museums and cafés?
check.hint: Städte means cities.
check.explanation: der Städtetrip = a city break.

check.prompt: Which type of holiday does Mira like best?
check.hint: She likes the mountains.
check.explanation: Mira macht am liebsten Wanderurlaub.

check.prompt: Write in German: I do not feel like swimming today.
answers: Ich habe keine Lust, heute zu schwimmen.
Ich habe heute keine Lust, zu schwimmen.
Heute habe ich keine Lust, zu schwimmen.
check.hint: Use keine Lust; zu stands directly before swimming.
check.explanation: Ich habe keine Lust, heute zu schwimmen.

check.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Habt ihr Zeit, im Juli zu fahren?
Habt ihr Zeit, im Juli fahren?
Habt ihr Zeit zu im Juli fahren?
check.hint: zu stands right before the last verb.
check.explanation: Habt ihr Zeit, im Juli zu fahren?

check.prompt: Build: It is fun for me to plan trips.
check.hint: Es first, then the verb, the person in the dative, Spaß; then the zu-part.
check.explanation: Es macht mir Spaß, Reisen zu planen.

check.prompt: Leon möchte Kajak ___.
check.hint: möchte is a modal verb.
check.explanation: After möchte there is no zu: Leon möchte Kajak fahren.

check.prompt: Ich habe ___ Lust, im Regen zu wandern. (I do NOT feel like it.)
check.hint: Lust is feminine and has no article here.
check.explanation: Ich habe keine Lust, im Regen zu wandern.

check.prompt: 'Hast du Lust zu kommen?' has no comma. Is that wrong?
options: Yes, the comma is always required.
No, with only zu + verb the comma is optional.
Yes, zu must stand before Lust.
check.hint: Look at how short the zu-part is.
check.explanation: A zu-part of only zu + verb may be written without a comma.

check.prompt: Build: Do you feel like going on holiday with us?
check.hint: A yes/no question starts with the verb; the zu-part with the verb comes last.
check.explanation: Hast du Lust, mit uns Urlaub zu machen?

lessons.title: Wir versuchen, früh loszufahren: zu after verbs and inside separable verbs
lessons.goal: Plan a trip and talk about intentions with versuchen, vergessen, anfangen, aufhören, vorhaben, beschließen and sich vornehmen + zu, and put zu inside separable verbs.

grammar.topic: zu + infinitive after verbs; zu inside separable verbs
grammar.point: After verbs like versuchen, vergessen, anfangen, aufhören, vorhaben, beschließen and sich vornehmen a zu-part follows after a comma. With separable verbs zu goes between prefix and verb and the verb is written as one word: anzurufen, loszufahren. After modal verbs and werden there is no zu.
grammar.oneLine: Ich vergesse nie, das Hotel anzurufen.

mistake.why: A separable verb takes zu inside: an + zu + rufen, written as one word. zu does not stand in front of it as a separate word.

terms.meaning: a verb with a prefix that moves away in a normal sentence: anrufen, losfahren, mitkommen
with separable verbs zu stands between prefix and verb: anzurufen, loszufahren
the verb form for the Perfekt: vergessen, angefangen, beschlossen

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Wir fahren früh los' to 'Wir versuchen, früh loszufahren'
cards.body: A trip needs planning: who books, who calls, who packs? In lesson 1 you used zu after Lust haben. Today the same little word zu works after verbs like versuchen and vergessen. And with separable verbs (anrufen, losfahren) zu moves inside the verb, so everything becomes one word: anzurufen.
steps: You already know: Ich rufe das Hotel an (separable verbs from A1) and Ich habe Lust, ans Meer zu fahren (zu after Lust, lesson 1).
New today: Ich vergesse nie, das Hotel anzurufen. After verbs like versuchen and vergessen a zu-part follows. With separable verbs zu goes inside: anzurufen.
By the end you can: talk about plans and intentions (versuchen, vorhaben, beschließen) and put zu into separable verbs.

examples.de: Ich rufe das Hotel an.
examples.en: I call the hotel.
examples.why: You know this already: a separable verb, the prefix at the end.

examples.de: Ich vergesse nie, das Hotel anzurufen.
examples.en: I never forget to call the hotel.
examples.why: New today: verb + comma + zu-part, and zu goes inside anrufen.

cards.more: A separable verb is like a zip. The two halves are an and rufen. In a normal sentence the zip is open: the verb is in one place and the prefix flies to the end: Ich rufe das Hotel an. In a zu-part you close the zip, and zu is the little zipper pull in the middle: an + zu + rufen = anzurufen. One word, nothing flies away. It looks strange for a day or two. After six or seven sentences your eyes will see it at once.

cards.title: Five steps to plan a trip
cards.body: Every trip has five steps: choose the destination (das Reiseziel), plan the route (die Route), fix the budget (das Budget), book the overnight stays (die Übernachtungen) and pack. On the way you can have a stopover (der Zwischenstopp). The WG goes through these steps for its July trip: Berlin – München – Innsbruck.
cards.lead: Before the new grammar, the WG needs a plan. This card gives you the five steps of trip planning and the new words you need for them, so the later examples make sense.

examples.de: Wir planen zuerst die Route.
examples.en: First we plan the route.

examples.de: Anna hat zwei Übernachtungen gebucht.
examples.en: Anna has booked two overnight stays.

examples.de: Wir machen einen Zwischenstopp in München.
examples.en: We make a stopover in Munich.

deeper.text: Words from the same family help you remember. übernachten means to stay overnight, and die Übernachtung is the stay itself, counted in nights: zwei Übernachtungen. festlegen means to fix or to set, for a date or a budget. The whole process has a name: die Reiseplanung. Planning a trip can be fun or stress, depending on the group.

example.de: Die Reiseplanung macht Anna Spaß.
example.en: Anna enjoys planning the trip.

cards.more: Picture the route on a paper map. Pin one is Berlin. Pin two is München, the stopover. Pin three is Innsbruck, the goal. Between the pins you need money, a bed for each night and a bag. These five steps are the same in every language, so you already know them. The only new thing is the German words for each step. Say the five steps aloud while you point at a pin: Reiseziel, Route, Budget, Übernachtungen, packen.
steps: 1. Reiseziel wählen: Wohin fahren wir?
2. Route planen: Berlin – München – Innsbruck
3. Budget festlegen: Wie viel Geld haben wir?
4. Übernachtungen buchen: Hütte, Zelt oder Hotel?
5. Packen: Rucksack, Regenjacke, Isomatte

cards.title: Seven verbs that take zu
cards.body: Seven verbs open a zu-part: versuchen (to try), vergessen (to forget), anfangen (to begin), aufhören (to stop), vorhaben (to plan), beschließen (to decide) and sich vornehmen (to resolve). The pattern is the same as with Lust: comma, the rest, then zu + infinitive at the end.
cards.lead: In lesson 1 nouns opened the zu-part. Now verbs do the same job. On this card you meet seven common ones, with the plan words from the last card, so you can talk about intentions.

examples.de: Wir versuchen, billige Übernachtungen zu finden.
examples.en: We are trying to find cheap overnight stays.

examples.de: Leon hat beschlossen, mit dem Zug zu fahren.
examples.en: Leon has decided to go by train.

examples.de: Mira hat vor, zwei Wochen in Österreich zu bleiben.
examples.en: Mira plans to stay in Austria for two weeks.

deeper.text: Do not mix up versuchen and probieren. versuchen goes with an action and zu: you try to do something. probieren goes with a thing: you taste a dish or test an idea. In careful German, Ich probiere, früh aufzustehen sounds odd. Say Ich versuche, früh aufzustehen. For food, probieren is right.

example.de: Willst du den Kuchen probieren?
example.en: Do you want to try the cake?

cards.more: English has the same group of verbs, only the little word is hidden. I try to find a hotel. I forget to call. I decide to go. I begin to plan. In English all of them have to, and in German all of them have zu. The difference: English also says I stop calling or I begin planning, with -ing. German always uses zu plus infinitive here. So translate the English to, and put it right in front of the last verb: zu.

rows: Anna versucht, ein günstiges Hotel zu finden.
Leon vergisst manchmal, Tickets zu kaufen.
Wir fangen an, die Reise zu planen.
Ben hört auf, vom Meer zu reden.
Mira hat vor, zwei Wochen zu bleiben.
Wir beschließen, mit dem Zug zu fahren.
Wir nehmen uns vor, nur eine Tasche zu packen.

cards.title: zu inside separable verbs
cards.body: A separable verb has two halves: an + rufen. In a zu-part, zu goes between the halves, and everything is written as one word: an + zu + rufen = anzurufen. The prefix (an, aus, los, mit) comes first and is stressed. The zu-part still stands at the end after the comma.
cards.lead: Many travel verbs are separable: anrufen, losfahren, mitkommen. This card shows how zu sneaks inside them, so you can say things like Vergiss nicht, anzurufen! correctly.

examples.de: Vergiss nicht, die Tickets auszudrucken.
examples.en: Do not forget to print out the tickets.

examples.de: Wir haben vor, um sechs Uhr loszufahren.
examples.en: We plan to set off at six o'clock.

examples.de: Hast du Lust, mitzukommen?
examples.en: Do you feel like coming along?

deeper.text: Verbs with an inseparable prefix (be-, ver-, ent-, er-) do not split, so zu stays outside, in front, as two words: zu besuchen, zu verstehen, zu beschließen. The test is simple: if the prefix flies to the end in a normal sentence (ich rufe an), zu goes inside. If not (ich besuche), zu stays in front.

example.de: Ich habe Lust, Freunde in München zu besuchen.
example.en: I feel like visiting friends in Munich.

cards.more: Think of a suitcase with two compartments, left and right. A separable verb lives in both: an on the left, rufen on the right. In a zu-part you slide a label between the compartments, and the label says zu. Then you close the case and write the whole word. If a verb has only one compartment, like besuchen, there is no gap, so the label goes outside, in front: zu besuchen. One question decides it: does the prefix fly away in a normal sentence?

rows: Ich vergesse oft, eine Jacke mitzunehmen.

steps: 1. The verb has two halves: an|rufen
2. Put zu between them: an + zu + rufen
3. Write it as one word: anzurufen
4. Keep it at the end after the comma: …, das Hotel anzurufen.

cards.title: No zu after modals and werden
cards.body: Modal verbs (können, müssen, wollen, dürfen, sollen, möchte) and werden never take zu. They send the second verb to the end of the same sentence, with no comma. Ask yourself: is the first verb a modal or werden? Then there is no zu. All other verbs from this lesson need zu.
cards.lead: You now know many verbs with zu. Here is the other side: the verbs that never take it. Putting them side by side stops you from adding zu everywhere.

examples.de: Wir müssen früh losfahren.
examples.en: We have to set off early.

examples.de: Wir versuchen, früh loszufahren.
examples.en: We are trying to set off early.

examples.de: Wir werden früh losfahren.
examples.en: We will set off early.

deeper.text: Two verbs sit in the middle. With helfen, a longer second part takes zu: Ben hilft Anna, das Gepäck zu tragen. With lernen, short phrases often have no zu: Ich lerne schwimmen. People say this every day, but with a longer part you use zu. When in doubt, a short phrase without zu is safe after lernen, and zu after helfen.

example.de: Ben hilft Anna, das Gepäck zu tragen.
example.en: Ben helps Anna to carry the luggage.

cards.more: Make two piles of verbs on a table. Pile one is small: können, müssen, wollen, dürfen, sollen, möchte and werden. These verbs are strong and need no help, so no zu. Pile two is big: versuchen, vergessen, anfangen, aufhören, vorhaben, beschließen, sich vornehmen and all the nouns like Lust. These need the little helper zu. A common slip is to add zu after a modal: Wir können morgen zu fahren. The right sentence is Wir können morgen fahren.

rows: können, müssen, wollen, dürfen, sollen, möchte

cards.title: Perfekt + zu-part
cards.body: In the Perfekt, nothing changes in the zu-part. The main verb is the participle at the end of the main clause. Then comes the comma and the zu-part with its own verb at the end: Ich habe vergessen, dich anzurufen. Never put the zu-part in front of the participle.
cards.lead: So far the main verbs were in the present. In real stories you talk about what happened: Ich habe vergessen … This card shows that the zu-part stays exactly as you learned.

examples.de: Ich habe vergessen, dich anzurufen.
examples.en: I forgot to call you.

examples.de: Wir haben angefangen, die Reise zu planen.
examples.en: We have started to plan the trip.

examples.de: Ben hat aufgehört, vom Meer zu reden.
examples.en: Ben has stopped talking about the sea.

deeper.text: Look at the participles in this lesson: versucht, vergessen, beschlossen. None of them has ge-. Verbs with the inseparable prefixes be-, ver- and ent- never take ge- in the Perfekt. Separable verbs put ge- inside, just like zu: angefangen, aufgehört, vorgenommen. So the same gap that takes zu also takes ge-.

example.de: Hast du vergessen, die Tickets zu kaufen?
example.en: Did you forget to buy the tickets?

cards.more: Imagine a sentence as two trains on two tracks. Train one is the main clause: Ich habe vergessen. It ends with the participle, then a comma, like a station. Train two is the zu-part: dich anzurufen. It starts after the station. Train two never drives in front of train one. This is why the participle stays in front of the comma. If you want to check your sentence, cover the zu-part with your hand: the first train must still make sense.
steps: 1. Main clause with the participle: Ich habe vergessen
2. Comma: ,
3. Rest of the information: dich
4. zu-form of the verb, at the end: anzurufen

cards.title: The WG group chat
cards.body: The WG plans the trip in a group chat. Read the messages and find every zu. You will see the seven verbs, a separable zu-form (anzurufen), a Perfekt sentence and a modal sentence without zu. Everything from this lesson sits in one conversation, like the chats you will read in real life.
cards.lead: This is the last card of the lesson. The WG uses all the patterns together in one chat, and you can practise reading them in a real situation.

examples.de: Ich habe vor, heute Abend die Route zu planen.
examples.en: I intend to plan the route this evening.

examples.de: Vergiss nicht, einen Zwischenstopp in München zu machen.
examples.en: Do not forget to make a stopover in Munich.

examples.de: Ich versuche, ein günstiges Hotel zu finden.
examples.en: I am trying to find a cheap hotel.

deeper.text: In chats you will see two handy chunks. Vergiss nicht, … zu …! is a friendly reminder. Was hast du vor? asks about plans. Here vorhaben has no zu, because there is no second verb after it. So the rule is: vorhaben + an action needs zu, but Was hast du vor? is a complete question and needs nothing more.

example.de: Was hast du im Juli vor?
example.en: What are you planning for July?

cards.more: Read the chat twice. The first time, ignore the grammar and find out who does what: Leon plans the route, Anna looks for a hotel, Mira reminds everyone, Ben stops talking about the sea. The second time, underline only the little words zu, and look at the word right after each zu: it is always the verb at the end. Then find the two sentences that have no zu at all. They are the modal ones.

rows: Ich habe vor, heute Abend die Route zu planen.
Super! Vergiss nicht, einen Zwischenstopp in München zu machen.
Ich versuche, ein günstiges Hotel zu finden.

Ich habe vergessen, Frau Weber anzurufen. Sie hat noch unser Zelt.
Wir müssen noch das Budget festlegen.

lessons.title: Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen: adjective + zu, and a planning talk
lessons.goal: Give your opinion about travel plans with Es ist + adjective + zu and Ich finde es + adjective + zu, and use all zu patterns in a planning talk.

grammar.topic: adjective + zu: Es ist wichtig, … zu …; Ich finde es …, … zu …
grammar.point: An adjective can open a zu-part: Es ist + adjective, comma, the rest, zu + infinitive at the end. With finden: Ich finde es + adjective, … zu … The es stands for the zu-part. With separable verbs zu goes inside: Es ist wichtig, eine Jacke mitzunehmen.
grammar.oneLine: Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen.

mistake.wrong: Es ist wichtig, zu eine Regenjacke mitnehmen.
mistake.right: Es ist wichtig, eine Regenjacke mitzunehmen.
mistake.why: zu does not stand right after the comma. With a separable verb it goes inside the verb at the end: mit + zu + nehmen = mitzunehmen.

terms.meaning: es that stands for the zu-part: Es ist wichtig, … zu …
advantage / disadvantage
the second part of the sentence after the comma, with zu + infinitive at the end

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Camping ist toll' to 'Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen'
cards.body: The WG argues about the plan: a tent, a hut in Tirol, or the sea? You can say Ich finde Camping toll and Ich habe Lust, im Zelt zu schlafen. Today you give your opinion about doing something, with a new frame: es ist + adjective, then a zu-part. At the end the WG tries to find a compromise.
steps: You already know: Ich finde Camping toll (opinions from A2) and Ich habe Lust, im Zelt zu schlafen (lesson 1).
New today: Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen. An adjective like toll, wichtig or gefährlich can open a zu-part after es ist.
By the end you can: give your opinion about travel plans and join a planning talk using every zu pattern from lessons 1 and 2.

examples.de: Ich finde Camping toll.
examples.en: I think camping is great.
examples.why: You know this already: an opinion with finden.

examples.de: Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen.
examples.en: It is great to sleep in a tent.
examples.why: New today: es ist + adjective + comma + zu-part.

cards.more: In lessons 1 and 2 the zu-part came after something with a verb or a noun: Lust haben, versuchen. Now the opinion word comes first. Imagine a street sign that says Wichtig! or Schön! or Gefährlich! The sign has no sentence yet. Es ist is the pole that holds the sign. Then the zu-part tells you what the sign is about: eine Regenjacke mitzunehmen. So you build your opinion like a sign on a pole, one card at a time.

cards.title: Es ist + adjective + zu
cards.body: An adjective can open a zu-part, too. The frame is Es ist + adjective, comma, the rest, zu + infinitive. Es is only a placeholder: the real subject is the zu-part. The adjective tells what you think about doing it: wichtig, schön, schwer, leicht, gefährlich, riskant, praktisch.
cards.lead: Until now the zu-part followed Lust, a noun or a verb. On this card an adjective starts it, so you can say whether something is important, nice, hard or dangerous.

examples.de: Es ist wichtig, eine Regenjacke mitzunehmen.
examples.en: It is important to take a rain jacket.

examples.de: Es ist gefährlich, bei Gewitter auf den Berg zu gehen.
examples.en: It is dangerous to go up the mountain in a thunderstorm.

examples.de: Es ist schön, früh am Morgen zu wandern.
examples.en: It is nice to hike early in the morning.

deeper.text: The word schwer has two meanings. With a thing it means heavy: Der Rucksack ist schwer. With an action it means difficult: Es ist schwer, mit wenig Gepäck zu reisen. The opposite of difficult is leicht, which also means light. Context tells you which meaning is right. The adjective has no ending here, because it stands after ist.

example.de: Es ist schwer, mit wenig Gepäck zu reisen.
example.en: It is hard to travel with little luggage.

cards.more: Think of a news headline with a mood: Wichtig! Gefährlich! Praktisch! The adjective is the mood sign. Then comes the story, and the story is a zu-part. Wichtig, eine Regenjacke mitzunehmen. If you only say Es ist wichtig, nobody knows what is important, so you always need the second part. Es ist the small word that makes the sentence complete, like a coat hanger that holds the heavy coat, the zu-part, at the end of the sentence.

rows: Es ist schön, am See zu sitzen.
Es ist leicht, mit dem Zug zu fahren.
Es ist gefährlich, bei Gewitter zu wandern.
Es ist riskant, bei Nebel zu wandern.
Es ist praktisch, einen kleinen Rucksack zu haben.

cards.title: Ich finde es + adjective + zu
cards.body: To give your own opinion, use finden: Ich finde es + adjective, comma, zu-part. Es stands for the zu-part and must stay. You know Ich finde, dass …, which says the same in another build. Both are correct. The zu version is shorter when you do the thing yourself.
cards.lead: On the last card the adjective was a fact. Now it becomes your opinion: you say what you find boring, restful or exhausting. This is the most useful pattern for planning talks.

examples.de: Ich finde es langweilig, am Strand zu liegen.
examples.en: I find it boring to lie on the beach.

examples.de: Anna findet es erholsam, abends im Café zu sitzen.
examples.en: Anna finds it restful to sit in a café in the evening.

examples.de: Leon findet es anstrengend, jeden Tag zu packen.
examples.en: Leon finds it exhausting to pack every day.

deeper.text: The es is a placeholder for the zu-part. In more formal or written German you can move the zu-part to the front, and then es disappears: Im Zelt zu schlafen ist toll. The meaning does not change. In speaking, the version with es is more common, so use that one yourself, and recognise the other one when you read.

example.de: Im Zelt zu schlafen ist toll.
example.en: Sleeping in a tent is great.

cards.more: Compare three ways to say the same opinion, like three roads to the same town. Road one: Ich finde, dass Camping toll ist. It has the word dass and the verb at the end. Road two: Ich finde es toll, im Zelt zu schlafen. It has es and a zu-part. Road three: Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen. It starts with es ist. All three get you there. Choose the road you feel safe on, but try the other two once, so your ears know them.

rows: Ich finde, dass Camping toll ist.
Ich finde es toll, im Zelt zu schlafen.
Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen.

cards.title: Möglichkeit, Gelegenheit, Mut + zu
cards.body: Three more nouns open a zu-part, like Lust and Idee: die Möglichkeit (possibility), die Gelegenheit (opportunity) and der Mut (courage). Unlike Lust they come with an article: die Möglichkeit, die Gelegenheit, den Mut. Use them with haben. After the comma comes the same zu-part as before.
cards.lead: In lesson 1 you used Lust, Zeit, Spaß and Idee. This card adds three nouns that sound more grown-up and that you will meet in texts about travel and plans.

examples.de: Auf der Hütte hat man die Möglichkeit, den Sonnenaufgang zu sehen.
examples.en: At the hut you have the chance to see the sunrise.

examples.de: Leon hat den Mut, im Fluss zu baden.
examples.en: Leon has the courage to swim in the river.

examples.de: Wir haben die Gelegenheit, eine Nacht auf der Hütte zu schlafen.
examples.en: We have the opportunity to sleep one night at the hut.

deeper.text: The two words are close, but not the same. Die Möglichkeit says that something is possible. Die Gelegenheit is a good moment that may not come again, so it sounds more special. Leon can say Das ist die Gelegenheit when the weather is perfect for a hike. Both take haben and a zu-part.

example.de: Das ist die Gelegenheit, die Alpen zu sehen.
example.en: This is the opportunity to see the Alps.

cards.more: Picture three little signs on a mountain path. The first sign says Möglichkeit: a path is open, you may go. The second sign says Gelegenheit: the path is open today, and the weather is perfect, so go now. The third sign says Mut: the path is steep, and you need courage. All three signs lead to the same viewpoint, the zu-part. You take the path with haben: Man hat die Möglichkeit. Wir haben die Gelegenheit. Leon hat den Mut.

rows: Man hat die Möglichkeit, früh zu starten.
Wir haben die Gelegenheit, Tirol zu sehen.
Ben hat den Mut, auf den Gipfel zu klettern.

cards.title: Pros and cons of a hut holiday
cards.body: Use all the patterns to weigh a plan. A Hütte is a simple house in the mountains, often with a Schlafsaal, a shared room with many beds. Make two columns: Vorteil (advantage) and Nachteil (disadvantage). Each point is one sentence with zu, or with weil. This is how you prepare a planning talk.
cards.lead: You can now build every kind of zu-part. This card puts them into a pros-and-cons list for a hut holiday in Tirol, so you can practise giving reasons.

examples.de: Es ist ungewöhnlich, im Schlafsaal zu schlafen.
examples.en: It is unusual to sleep in a dormitory.

examples.de: Es ist nicht bequem, mit vielen Leuten in einem Zimmer zu schlafen.
examples.en: It is not comfortable to sleep in one room with many people.

examples.de: Man hat die Möglichkeit, den Sternenhimmel zu sehen.
examples.en: You have the chance to see the starry sky.

deeper.text: German often builds the opposite with un-: bequem and unbequem, gewöhnlich and ungewöhnlich. So Es ist nicht bequem and Es ist unbequem mean the same, but the second one is a bit stronger and shorter. Both work with a zu-part. This is a good habit for B1: learn a word together with its un- opposite.

example.de: Es ist unbequem, im Zelt zu sitzen.
example.en: It is uncomfortable to sit in a tent.

cards.more: A pros-and-cons list is like a seesaw with two seats. On the left seat you put the good points, on the right seat the bad ones. Then you look at which side goes down. The frames you know do the work: Es ist … , … zu … for opinions, Man hat die Möglichkeit, … zu … for chances, weil … for reasons. You do not need new grammar. You only need to choose a frame for each point, like picking a tool from a box.

rows: Es ist ungewöhnlich, im Schlafsaal zu schlafen.
Es ist nicht bequem, mit vielen Leuten in einem Zimmer zu schlafen.
Man hat die Möglichkeit, den Sternenhimmel zu sehen.
Es ist anstrengend, den Rucksack nach oben zu tragen.
Es ist schön, abends am Lagerfeuer zu sitzen.
Wir haben keine Zeit, lange auszuschlafen, weil das Frühstück früh ist.

cards.title: The planning talk
cards.body: Now the WG talks about the hut. Mira proposes, Ben is not sure, Anna and Leon bring their points, and in the end they look for a compromise. Read the ten lines and find all four patterns: noun + zu, verb + zu, adjective + zu and a separable zu-form. One more fixed phrase: Das ist mal was anderes!
cards.lead: This is the central card of the lesson. The patterns of lessons 1 to 3 meet in one real talk, with different opinions and a reason with weil.

examples.de: Ich finde es langweilig, nur zu wandern.
examples.en: I find it boring to only hike.

examples.de: Es ist wichtig, früh loszufahren, weil das Wetter am Nachmittag oft schlecht ist.
examples.en: It is important to set off early because the weather is often bad in the afternoon.

examples.de: Wir versuchen, einen Kompromiss zu finden.
examples.en: We are trying to find a compromise.

deeper.text: Das ist mal was anderes! means that is something different for a change. It can be a compliment (new and exciting) or a polite doubt, depending on your voice. Native speakers say it all the time when someone has a new idea. Learn it as one chunk, and do not translate it word by word.

example.de: Ein Urlaub auf einer Hütte? Das ist mal was anderes!
example.en: A holiday at a hut? That is something different!

cards.more: Read the talk like a football match with four players. First, only follow the story: who wants what? Then watch each player's moves. Mira uses Idee + zu. Ben uses Ich finde es + adjective + zu. Anna uses Ich finde es schön + zu and Es macht Spaß + zu. Ben finally uses Mut + zu. Leon uses Gelegenheit + zu and nicht leicht + zu. Last, count the little word zu: you should find it nine or ten times. Each zu has a verb right behind it. That is your safety net.

rows: Ich habe die Idee, eine Woche in Tirol zu wandern und auf Hütten zu schlafen.
Ich finde es langweilig, nur zu wandern. Ich habe Lust aufs Meer!
Ein Urlaub auf einer Hütte? Das ist mal was anderes! Ich finde es schön, abends am Lagerfeuer zu sitzen.
Wir haben die Gelegenheit, im Juli zwei Wochen zu fahren. Es ist ungewöhnlich, so viel Zeit zu haben!
Es ist wichtig, früh loszufahren, weil das Wetter am Nachmittag oft schlecht ist.
Gibt es in Tirol einen See? Dann habe ich Lust, mitzukommen.
Ja, neben der Hütte gibt es einen See. Es macht Spaß, im See zu schwimmen.
Es ist nicht leicht, im Juli eine Hütte zu finden. Wir müssen bald buchen.
Na gut. Ich habe den Mut, einmal auf einen Gipfel zu klettern.
Wir versuchen, einen Kompromiss zu finden.

cards.title: Your speaking frame
cards.body: Use this four-step frame to speak for half a minute about a travel plan. Say what you feel like doing, then your opinion with Ich finde es, then a reason with weil, and finally a suggestion with Wir könnten …, which you know from Konjunktiv II. Practise it aloud, with a timer if you like.
cards.lead: This last card turns the whole lesson into a speaking tool. Four short steps give you a mini speech that you can use in class, in a chat or on a trip.

examples.de: Ich habe Lust, eine Woche in den Bergen zu wandern.
examples.en: I feel like hiking in the mountains for a week.

examples.de: Ich finde es toll, im Zelt zu schlafen, weil es billig ist.
examples.en: I think it is great to sleep in a tent, because it is cheap.

examples.de: Wir könnten zwei Nächte auf einer Hütte schlafen.
examples.en: We could sleep two nights at a hut.

deeper.text: Ich habe Lust is friendly and casual. A softer way to say what you wish is the Konjunktiv II you know: Ich würde gern auf einer Hütte schlafen. Both are good. Use Lust haben with friends, and würde gern with people you do not know well. Notice that würde gern needs no zu: it is a wish with a helper verb, like a modal.

example.de: Ich würde gern auf einer Hütte schlafen.
example.en: I would like to sleep at a hut.

cards.more: Think of a four-step staircase. Step one is your wish: Ich habe Lust. Step two is your opinion: Ich finde es schön. Step three is your reason: weil. Step four is your offer: Wir könnten. When you speak, you climb one step at a time, and you never have to jump. If you forget a word, stay on the step and say a simpler sentence. The listener will wait for you. That is how real conversations feel.
steps: 1. Ich habe (keine) Lust, … zu …
2. Ich finde es …, … zu …
3. … weil …
4. Wir könnten …

drills.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Es ist wichtig, zu eine Regenjacke mitnehmen.
Es ist wichtig, eine Regenjacke mitnehmen zu.
Es ist wichtig, eine Regenjacke mitzunehmen.
drills.hint: A separable verb takes zu inside, and the verb is last.
drills.explanation: mit + zu + nehmen = mitzunehmen.

drills.prompt: Es ist schön, früh am Morgen ___. (aufstehen)
drills.hint: Put zu between the prefix and the verb and write one word.
drills.explanation: Es ist schön, früh am Morgen aufzustehen.

drills.prompt: Build: I find it boring to lie on the beach.
drills.hint: Ich finde es + adjective, comma, the rest, zu + verb last.
drills.explanation: Ich finde es langweilig, am Strand zu liegen.

drills.prompt: In 'Ich finde es toll, im Zelt zu schlafen', what does es stand for?
drills.hint: es is a placeholder.
drills.explanation: es stands for the zu-part: im Zelt zu schlafen.

drills.prompt: Write in German: It is important to leave early.
drills.hint: Es ist + adjective, comma, then the zu-form of losfahren.
drills.explanation: Es ist wichtig, früh loszufahren.

drills.prompt: Leon hat den Mut, im Fluss ___.
drills.hint: Where does zu go?
drills.explanation: zu stands before the infinitive: im Fluss zu baden.

blind.prompt: Write in German: It is not easy to travel with little luggage.
answers: Es ist nicht leicht, mit wenig Gepäck zu reisen.
Es ist nicht einfach, mit wenig Gepäck zu reisen.
blind.hint: Es ist nicht + adjective, comma, then the zu-part with the verb last.
blind.explanation: Es ist nicht leicht, mit wenig Gepäck zu reisen.

check.prompt: Es ist ___, bei Gewitter auf den Berg zu gehen. (dangerous)
check.hint: Think of the danger of lightning.
check.explanation: gefährlich = dangerous.

check.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Ich finde es toll, im Zelt zu schlafen.
Ich finde es toll, zu im Zelt schlafen.
Ich finde es toll, im Zelt schlafen.
check.hint: Look for es and for zu.
check.explanation: Ich finde es + adjective, comma, zu-part.

check.prompt: Write in German: It is nice to sit by the campfire in the evening.
answers: Es ist schön, abends am Lagerfeuer zu sitzen.
Es ist schön, am Abend am Lagerfeuer zu sitzen.
check.hint: Es ist + adjective, comma, then the zu-part with the verb last.
check.explanation: Es ist schön, abends am Lagerfeuer zu sitzen.

check.prompt: Build: Mira has the opportunity to see the sunrise.
check.hint: haben + noun, comma, the rest, zu + verb.
check.explanation: Mira hat die Gelegenheit, den Sonnenaufgang zu sehen.

check.prompt: Ich habe Lust, Freunde ___.
check.hint: besuchen is not separable: does zu go inside?
check.explanation: besuchen has an inseparable prefix, so zu stays in front: zu besuchen.

check.prompt: Vergiss nicht, Mira ___. (anrufen)
check.hint: Put zu between the prefix and the verb and write one word.
check.explanation: Vergiss nicht, Mira anzurufen.

check.prompt: Wir wollen im Juli nach Tirol ___.
check.hint: wollen is a modal verb.
check.explanation: After a modal verb there is no zu: Wir wollen im Juli nach Tirol fahren.

check.prompt: What is der Schlafsaal?
options: a big room with many beds
check.hint: schlafen = to sleep, der Saal = hall.
check.explanation: der Schlafsaal = dormitory.

check.prompt: 'Im Zelt zu schlafen ist toll.' means the same as …
options: Es ist toll, im Zelt schlafen.
Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen.
Ich finde im Zelt zu schlafen es toll.

check.explanation: Es ist toll, im Zelt zu schlafen. = Im Zelt zu schlafen ist toll.

check.hint: Build the opposite of bequem with a short prefix.
check.explanation: Es ist unbequem, im Schlafsaal zu schlafen.

lessons.title: Wir buchen das Angebot, weil es günstig ist: travel offers and verb-final review
lessons.goal: Read and compare travel offers, give reasons and opinions, and review the verb at the end after weil, dass and wenn (also with modal, Perfekt, separable verbs and the side clause first).

grammar.topic: Verb at the end: weil, dass, wenn (review)
grammar.point: After weil, dass and wenn the verb with the person ending goes to the end of its clause: modal last (…, dass wir buchen müssen), helper last in Perfekt (…, weil Anna gebucht hat), separable verb in one piece (…, wenn der Zug ankommt). If the side clause comes first, the main verb follows right after the comma.
grammar.oneLine: Wenn wir früh buchen, bekommen wir einen Rabatt.

mistake.why: weil sends the verb with the person ending to the end of the clause, so the helper haben goes last.

terms.meaning: a clause that starts with weil, dass, wenn or ob; its verb stands at the end
package holiday: transport, hotel and often meals in one price

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Das ist günstig' to '…, weil das Angebot günstig ist'
cards.body: Anna has two holiday offers open on her laptop and cannot decide. To compare them she needs reasons, opinions and conditions, and all three send the verb to the end of the clause. You already do this with weil. Today you repeat the rule with weil, dass and wenn and use it on real travel offers.
steps: You already know: Ich finde die Reise gut, weil sie billig ist. After weil the verb goes to the end (A2 chapter 1).
New today: the same rule with dass and wenn, with modal verbs and Perfekt, and when the side clause comes first. Plus the words of a travel offer.
By the end you can: read a travel offer, compare two offers and give reasons and opinions.

examples.de: Ich finde die Reise gut, weil sie billig ist.
examples.en: I think the trip is good because it is cheap.
examples.why: You know this already.

examples.de: Wenn wir früh buchen, bekommen wir einen Frühbucherrabatt.
examples.en: If we book early, we get an early-booking discount.
examples.why: New today: wenn-clause first, the verb waits at the end, then the main verb.

examples.de: Ich glaube, dass Halbpension reicht.
examples.en: I think half board is enough.
examples.why: New today: an opinion with dass.

cards.more: Think of a train leaving the station. The little word weil, dass or wenn is the engine, and the other words are the carriages. The verb is always the last carriage, wherever the train goes. You have driven this train before with weil. Today you learn that it also runs with dass and wenn, with two verbs on board, and with the engine at the front of the whole sentence. We go step by step.

cards.title: Reading a travel offer
cards.body: A travel offer is a small table of facts. Learn its labels: Reiseziel (destination), Dauer (length), Unterkunft (where you sleep), Verpflegung (meals) and Preis pro Person. Halbpension means breakfast and dinner, Vollpension all meals. inklusive means already in the price; an Aufpreis is an extra charge.
cards.lead: Anna's two offers are on the table. Before we give any reasons, we read them and learn the labels that every offer uses: destination, length, meals, price and what costs extra.

examples.de: Das Reiseangebot „Strand & Stadt“ dauert sieben Nächte in Lissabon.
examples.en: The travel offer 'Beach & City' lasts seven nights in Lisbon.

examples.de: Die Unterkunft ist ein Hotel, und Halbpension ist inklusive.
examples.en: The accommodation is a hotel, and half board is included.

examples.de: Die Hüttenwoche in Tirol kostet 540 Euro pro Person.
examples.en: The hut week in Tirol costs 540 euros per person.

examples.de: Der Transfer vom Flughafen kostet 30 Euro Aufpreis.
examples.en: The transfer from the airport costs 30 euros extra.

deeper.text: A Pauschalreise (package holiday) bundles transport, hotel and often meals into one price. Ads often show a price with ab (from): ab 649 Euro is the cheapest date and room, not the price for everybody. So Germans always check two things: what is inklusive and what carries an Aufpreis. The small print decides whether an offer is really günstig.

example.de: Der Preis ab 649 Euro ist der Preis pro Person im Doppelzimmer.
example.en: The price from 649 euros is the price per person in a double room.

cards.more: Think of a phone contract. The big number on the poster is not the whole story, so you read the small print for what is included and what costs extra. A travel offer works the same way. Reiseziel and Dauer are the big picture, Unterkunft and Verpflegung are your bed and your meals, and the last line is the price per person. Always read two words twice: inklusive means already paid, Aufpreis means you pay more.

cards.title: Verb at the end: weil, dass, wenn
cards.body: After weil, dass and wenn the verb goes to the end of its clause. With two verbs, the one with the person ending goes last: the modal (müssen) or the helper (hat). A separable verb joins up again: ankommt. Say the clause in your head and check: does it end with a verb?
cards.lead: Now the offers are on the table. Next we repeat the one rule that every reason sentence needs: what happens to the verbs after weil, dass and wenn, even when there are two or more.

examples.de: Wir buchen, weil das Angebot günstig ist.
examples.en: We are booking because the offer is cheap.

examples.de: Anna sagt, dass wir früh buchen müssen.
examples.en: Anna says we have to book early.

examples.de: Wir fahren nach Portugal, weil Anna schon gebucht hat.
examples.en: We are going to Portugal because Anna has already booked.

examples.de: Ich rufe dich an, wenn der Zug ankommt.
examples.en: I'll call you when the train arrives.

deeper.text: Do not mix up dass and das. dass (two s) opens a side clause, so a verb waits at the end. das (one s) is a normal word meaning the or that, and it moves no verb. A quick test: if you can replace it with dieses or welches, it is das. If not, write dass. The video of this lesson trains exactly this.

example.de: Ich glaube, dass das Hotel gut ist.
example.en: I think that the hotel is good.

cards.more: Imagine a train leaving the platform. The word weil, dass or wenn is the engine, the subject and the other words are carriages, and the verb is the last carriage with the red light. It always stays at the back. If two verbs travel together, the one with the person ending takes the very last place and the other sits just in front. Nothing may come behind the last carriage, not even a time word like morgen.
steps: 1 weil / dass / wenn opens a side clause, then the subject comes.
2 The verb with the person ending goes to the very end: …, weil es günstig ist.
3 Modal: …, dass wir früh buchen müssen. Perfekt: …, weil Anna gebucht hat.
4 Separable verb: one word again at the end: …, wenn der Zug ankommt.

cards.title: Side clause first: verb, comma, verb
cards.body: A side clause can also open the sentence. It then counts as position one, so the verb of the main clause comes right after the comma. The two verbs meet at the comma: Wenn wir im Mai buchen, ist es billiger. The comma is always there, in both orders.
cards.lead: You can also start with the reason. This card shows what happens at the comma when the side clause comes first, a spot where many learners slip.

examples.de: Wenn wir im Mai buchen, ist es billiger.
examples.en: If we book in May, it is cheaper.

examples.de: Weil Ben das Meer liebt, möchte er nach Portugal.
examples.en: Because Ben loves the sea, he wants to go to Portugal.

examples.de: Wenn Anna Zeit hat, bucht sie das Hotel.
examples.en: When Anna has time, she books the hotel.

examples.de: Wenn das Wetter schlecht ist, bleiben wir im Hotel.
examples.en: If the weather is bad, we stay in the hotel.

deeper.text: Starting with the side clause puts the condition or reason first and gives it weight, like a drum roll before the news. Notice what the change does to the main clause: its subject now stands after the verb (ist es, möchte er), because the whole side clause already filled position one. Germans use this order a lot for conditions with wenn.

example.de: Wenn Mira anruft, kommt Leon sofort.
example.en: When Mira calls, Leon comes right away.

cards.more: Say it aloud like a drum beat: verb, comma, verb. Wenn wir im Mai buchen, ist es billiger. If you hear two verbs next to each other at the comma, the sentence is right. If a subject follows the comma, as in Wenn wir buchen, wir bekommen, something is missing, because the main verb must jump in right behind the comma. Listen for the double beat and you will hear your mistakes.

cards.title: Comparing offers: reasons and opinions
cards.body: To compare, mix a comparative with a reason: Das Angebot A ist besser, weil die Verpflegung inklusive ist. To say what you think, use Ich glaube, dass … or Ich finde, dass … The verb goes to the end of the dass-clause, as before.
cards.lead: With the rule in place we start using it. Here we compare the two offers with a comparative plus a reason, and with a few ways to say what you think.

examples.de: Das Angebot A ist besser, weil die Verpflegung inklusive ist.
examples.en: Offer A is better because the meals are included.

examples.de: Ich glaube, dass die Pauschalreise zu teuer ist.
examples.en: I think the package holiday is too expensive.

examples.de: Ben glaubt, dass Lissabon schöner ist.
examples.en: Ben thinks Lisbon is nicer.

examples.de: Wenn wir Vollpension buchen, brauchen wir kein Restaurant.
examples.en: If we book full board, we don't need a restaurant.

deeper.text: The opinion phrases differ in strength. Ich glaube, dass … is soft and open, Ich finde, dass … says this is my view, Ich bin sicher, dass … is strong. In everyday speech Germans often drop dass and keep normal word order: Ich glaube, das Hotel ist gut. Both are correct, but with dass the verb must go to the end.

example.de: Ich glaube, das Hotel ist gut.
example.en: I think the hotel is good.

cards.more: Imagine a judge with a score card. First comes the verdict: Angebot A ist besser. Then the evidence, introduced by weil: die Verpflegung ist inklusive. Last comes your own opinion, introduced by dass: Ich glaube, dass die Pauschalreise zu teuer ist. Verdict, evidence, opinion are three small jobs, and the evidence and the opinion both end with their verb. Build every comparison in this order and it sounds clear and confident.

cards.title: Booking and cancelling
cards.body: You book (buchen) a trip, and the booking is die Buchung. If you cancel it, you stornieren it, and a late cancellation can cost a Stornogebühr. An Ermäßigung is a reduction, and die Abreise is the day you leave. All of this fits the same side-clause patterns.
cards.lead: Offers get booked and sometimes cancelled. This card gives you the words for booking, cancelling and fees, all inside the side-clause patterns you have just practised.

examples.de: Wenn wir die Buchung stornieren, kostet es 50 Euro.
examples.en: If we cancel the booking, it costs 50 euros.

examples.de: Anna hat die Reise gestern gebucht.
examples.en: Anna booked the trip yesterday.

examples.de: Ben fragt, ob es eine Ermäßigung für Studenten gibt.
examples.en: Ben asks whether there is a reduction for students.

examples.de: Die Buchung ist fest, weil Anna schon bezahlt hat.
examples.en: The booking is firm because Anna has already paid.

deeper.text: German travel ads love two words. Frühbucher means early booker: a Frühbucherrabatt rewards you if you book months ahead. Last-Minute is borrowed from English and means a cheap leftover offer shortly before departure. Both save money, but in opposite ways: one needs planning, the other needs flexibility. Read the ad carefully to see which one it is.

example.de: Wenn man früh bucht, bekommt man einen Frühbucherrabatt.
example.en: If you book early, you get an early-booking discount.

cards.more: Think of a gym membership or a cinema ticket. The earlier you cancel, the less it costs, and the later you cancel, the more you pay. A travel booking works the same way. Buchen is the yes, stornieren is the no, and die Stornogebühr is the price of changing your mind. Ermäßigung is the opposite of Aufpreis: the first makes the price smaller, the second makes it bigger. Match each word with a small picture and it sticks.

cards.title: In the Reisebüro: a booking talk
cards.body: In a Reisebüro you use Sie. Anna asks, the employee offers. Learn three chunks you can reuse: Was ist im Preis inklusive? and pro Person and Ich hätte gern … Read the talk twice: once for the meaning, once to find the verb at the end of every side clause.
cards.lead: Now everything comes together in a real talk. Anna visits a Reisebüro, chooses meals, asks what is included and hears about a discount, using weil, wenn and the offer words.

examples.de: Guten Tag, ich möchte eine Pauschalreise nach Lissabon buchen.
examples.en: Anna: Hello, I would like to book a package holiday to Lisbon.

examples.de: Gern. Möchten Sie Halbpension oder Vollpension?
examples.en: Employee: Gladly. Would you like half board or full board?

examples.de: Halbpension reicht, weil wir mittags gern in der Stadt essen.
examples.en: Anna: Half board is enough because we like eating in town at lunchtime.

examples.de: Wenn Sie vor dem 1. Mai buchen, bekommen Sie einen Frühbucherrabatt.
examples.en: Employee: If you book before 1 May, you get an early-booking discount.

examples.de: Was ist im Preis inklusive?

lessons.title: Da der Zug günstiger ist, fahren wir mit der Bahn: da or weil?
lessons.goal: Give a known reason with da (usually at the start), answer Warum? with weil, and choose between train and plane with reasons.

grammar.point: da also means because: the verb goes to the end of the da-clause, and the da-clause usually comes first (Da der Zug voll ist, nehmen wir den nächsten.). weil answers Warum?; da gives a reason everybody knows. denn keeps normal word order. Watch out: da ist … means there, and the verb stays second.
grammar.oneLine: Da der Zug günstiger ist, fahren wir mit der Bahn.

mistake.wrong: Da ist der Zug günstiger, fahren wir mit der Bahn.
mistake.right: Da der Zug günstiger ist, fahren wir mit der Bahn.
mistake.why: da = because sends the verb to the end of its clause; da ist … means there.

terms.meaning: a known reason; verb at the end, clause usually first
high season / low season

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Weil der Zug billiger ist' to 'Da der Zug billiger ist, …'
cards.body: The WG argues: train or plane? Ben wants to fly, Mira wants the night train. Everybody gives reasons, and German has a second word for a reason that everybody already knows: da. It works like weil, but it usually stands at the start of the sentence. Today you learn when to choose da and when weil.
steps: You already know: Wir fahren mit dem Zug, weil er billiger ist. weil sends the verb to the end, and you can start with the side clause (lesson 4).
New today: da also means because. It sends the verb to the end, too, and usually opens the sentence. But da ist … means there!
By the end you can: choose between da, weil and denn and argue for train or plane.

examples.de: Wir fahren mit dem Zug, weil er billiger ist.
examples.en: We go by train because it is cheaper.
examples.why: You know this already.

examples.de: Da es in der Hauptsaison voll ist, fahren wir im Juni.
examples.en: Since it is crowded in high season, we travel in June.
examples.why: New today: da opens the sentence, the verb of the da-clause is last.

examples.de: Da ist der Bahnhof.
examples.en: There is the station.
examples.why: Careful: here da means there, and the verb stays in second place.

cards.more: Think of two friends in a kitchen. One says weil and gives a new reason: Weil es billiger ist! The other says da and mentions something that everyone in the room already knows: Da es regnet, bleiben wir hier. Both reasons work, but da sounds a little more written, like a note on the fridge. And da has a twin, the little word for there, which sends no verb away. We meet both twins slowly.

cards.title: Train or plane?
cards.body: Before the reasons, we need facts. A Bahnfahrt can be cheap with a Sparpreis. A Nachtzug has a Liegewagen where you sleep. It is klimafreundlich. A Flug has a short Flugzeit, but the way to the airport also takes time. Compare four things: price, time, environment, luggage.
cards.lead: The intro set up the choice between train and plane. First we collect the facts and the new words for the comparison, because a good reason needs good facts.

examples.de: Im Liegewagen kann man im Zug schlafen.
examples.en: In the couchette car you can sleep on the train.

examples.de: Die Bahnfahrt ist klimafreundlich.
examples.en: The train journey is climate-friendly.

examples.de: Mit dem Sparpreis ist die Fahrt nach München günstig.
examples.en: With the saver fare the journey to Munich is cheap.

examples.de: Die Flugzeit nach Lissabon ist kurz.
examples.en: The flight time to Lisbon is short.

deeper.text: A Sparpreis ticket is cheaper than a normal ticket, but it is usually tied to the one train you booked. A Flexpreis ticket costs more, and you may choose any train. So cheap and flexible rarely come together. When you compare a train with a plane, check not only the price but also whether you can still change your plan.

example.de: Mit dem Sparpreis dürfen wir nur diesen Zug nehmen.
example.en: With the saver fare we may only take this train.

cards.more: Imagine two shopping baskets. In the train basket you find a cheap Sparpreis, a bed in the Liegewagen and a clean conscience, because the Nachtzug is klimafreundlich. In the plane basket you find a short Flugzeit and a long way to the airport. Neither basket is better by itself. You choose by what matters to you, and later you will explain your choice with a reason. First, fill both baskets with facts.

rows: often cheap, a suitcase can cost extra
longer, but you can sleep in the Nachtzug

cards.title: da means because
cards.body: da also gives a reason, like weil, and the verb goes to the end of the da-clause. The da-clause usually comes first, so the main verb follows right after the comma. Warning: you know da as there (Da ist der Bahnhof.). Then the verb stays in second place and there is no comma.
cards.lead: Now the new word itself. da behaves like weil, but it has a twin that means there, so this card shows both side by side and tells you how to spot the difference.

examples.de: Da der Nachtzug klimafreundlich ist, nehmen wir ihn.
examples.en: Since the night train is climate-friendly, we take it.

examples.de: Da Ben das Meer liebt, fliegen die beiden nach Lissabon.
examples.en: Since Ben loves the sea, the two of them fly to Lisbon.

examples.de: Da ist der Bahnhof.
examples.en: There is the station.

examples.de: Da kommt der Zug.
examples.en: Here comes the train.

deeper.text: Spot the twin by looking at the next word. If a verb follows da directly, it means there (Da kommt der Zug.). If a subject follows and the verb is at the end of the clause, da means because. In writing, the because-da usually opens the sentence. You will hear it in announcements and read it in letters, so recognise it first.

example.de: Da es regnet, bleiben wir im Hotel.
example.en: Since it is raining, we stay in the hotel.

cards.more: Meet two twins with the same name. Da-the-place is a pointing finger: Da ist der Bahnhof. Look, over there. It sends no verb anywhere. Da-the-reason is a speech bubble above a sentence: Da der Zug voll ist, … It pulls the verb to the end like weil does. To tell the twins apart, look at what comes after da. A verb straight after means finger. A subject and a verb at the end means bubble.

rows: Da der Zug voll ist, nehmen wir den nächsten.
verb at the end of the clause

cards.title: da or weil?
cards.body: Use weil when you answer Warum? or give a new, important reason. Use da when the reason is known to everybody and you only mention it. Rule of thumb: a short answer to Warum? always starts with Weil, never with Da. da usually opens a sentence; weil often follows the main clause.
cards.lead: Two words, one job: which one fits? This card gives you a simple rule of thumb that works in almost every situation.

examples.de: Warum fahrt ihr im Juni?
examples.en: Why are you travelling in June?

examples.de: Weil es dann billiger ist.
examples.en: Because it is cheaper then.

examples.de: Da es im August überfüllt ist, fahren wir im Juni.
examples.en: Since it is overcrowded in August, we travel in June.

examples.de: Wir fahren im Juni, weil es dann billiger ist.
examples.en: We travel in June because it is cheaper then.

deeper.text: In speech, many Germans use weil almost everywhere, and da can sound a little written or formal. But da is very common in announcements and letters: Da der Zug Verspätung hat, … You will meet this in lesson 9. For your own speaking, weil is always safe. For reading and listening, you need to recognise da as well.

example.de: Da der Zug Verspätung hat, fahren wir später.
example.en: Since the train is late, we travel later.

cards.more: Picture a quiz show. The host asks Warum? and you must buzz with Weil: that is the answer. Now picture a note on the fridge: Da wir keine Milch mehr haben, gehe ich einkaufen. Everybody in the flat already knows there is no milk, so the note simply mentions it with da. Weil is the answer on the buzzer. Da is the shared fact on the fridge door, and it likes to stand at the start.

rows: Wir fahren im Juni, weil es billiger ist.
Da es im August überfüllt ist, fahren wir im Juni.

cards.title: weil, da and denn compared
cards.body: weil and da send the verb to the end. denn does not: after denn the word order stays normal, subject then verb. denn never starts a sentence, it only joins two main clauses. Ben: Ich fahre mit, denn ich liebe Züge. All three mean because.
cards.lead: You know denn from A2. Now put all three words side by side and check where the verb stands after each one.

examples.de: Ich fahre mit, denn ich liebe Züge.
examples.en: I'm coming along, because I love trains.

examples.de: Ich fahre mit, weil ich Züge liebe.
examples.en: I'm coming along because I love trains.

examples.de: Da ich Züge liebe, fahre ich mit.
examples.en: Since I love trains, I'm coming along.

examples.de: Mira bleibt zu Hause, denn sie hat keine Zeit.
examples.en: Mira stays at home, because she has no time.

deeper.text: denn is a pure connector: nothing can stand before it, and it cannot answer Warum? on its own. Another difference to weil: in speech, many Germans say weil and then use the normal order (Ich komme nicht, weil ich habe keine Zeit). You will hear this often, but it is not accepted in writing or in exams, so keep the verb at the end with weil.

example.de: Ich komme nicht, denn ich habe keine Zeit.
example.en: I'm not coming, because I have no time.

cards.more: Think of a bridge and two tunnels. denn is a bridge: you walk over it and the sentence continues just as before, subject then verb. weil and da are tunnels: when you enter, the verb gets pulled through to the other end. The word is different, but all three lead to the same place: a reason. Before you speak, ask yourself: bridge or tunnel? That one question gives you the right word order every time.

cards.title: Seasons and prices
cards.body: Prices depend on the season. In der Hauptsaison everything is teurer, ausgebucht (full) and überfüllt (too crowded). In der Nebensaison it is ruhiger and günstiger. For decisions use the chunk Das lohnt sich (nicht). It means it is (not) worth it.
cards.lead: Reasons about trains and planes often come down to prices, and prices come down to seasons. This card gives you the words for high and low season and for saying that something is worth it.

examples.de: Da im Juli alles ausgebucht ist, lohnt es sich, früh zu buchen.
examples.en: Since everything is fully booked in July, it is worth booking early.

examples.de: In der Hauptsaison ist es überall überfüllt.
examples.en: In high season it is overcrowded everywhere.

examples.de: Die Nebensaison ist günstiger, weil weniger Leute reisen.
examples.en: The low season is cheaper because fewer people travel.

examples.de: Das lohnt sich nicht.
examples.en: That is not worth it.

deeper.text: The high season depends on the region. At the sea it is summer. In the Alps there are two: summer for hiking and winter for skiing. So in Tirol, July and August are expensive, and so are Christmas and February. If you want a cheap holiday there, look for the weeks in between, for example in May or October.

example.de: In Tirol gibt es im Sommer und im Winter Hauptsaison.
example.en: In Tirol there is high season in summer and in winter.

cards.more: Think of a bakery. On Saturday morning there is a queue to the door and the best rolls are gone: that is Hauptsaison, überfüllt and ausgebucht. On Tuesday afternoon you are alone with the baker and everything is fresh and cheap: that is Nebensaison. A holiday town works like that bakery. Das lohnt sich means the queue is worth it, or the cheap quiet Tuesday is the better deal. Das lohnt sich nicht means skip it.

rows: Da es günstig ist, lohnt es sich.

cards.title: WG talk: train or plane?
cards.body: Four friends, one decision. Ben and Anna fly to Lisbon in the first week, and Mira and Leon take the night train to Tirol. Look for weil, da and denn. Which one answers Warum? Which one opens a sentence? Then read the talk aloud with a friend.
cards.lead: Now everything comes together in a real WG argument. You will meet weil, da and denn in one short talk and see which one each person chooses.

examples.de: Mira, warum fahrt ihr mit dem Nachtzug nach Innsbruck?
examples.en: Ben: Mira, why are you taking the night train to Innsbruck?

examples.de: Weil der Nachtzug klimafreundlich ist.
examples.en: Mira: Because the night train is climate-friendly.

examples.de: Aber der Flug ist schneller!
examples.en: Ben: But the flight is faster!

examples.de: Da wir Zeit haben, ist das kein Problem.
examples.en: Leon: Since we have time, that is no problem.

examples.de: Da Lissabon weit weg ist, fliegen Ben und ich.
examples.en: Anna: Since Lisbon is far away, Ben and I are flying.

examples.de: Wir fliegen in der ersten Woche, denn danach sind die Flüge teurer.
examples.en: Ben: We fly in the first week, because the flights are more expensive after that.

examples.de: Gut, dann fahren Leon und ich mit dem Zug.
examples.en: Mira: Good, then Leon and I go by train.

examples.de: Perfekt! Das lohnt sich für alle.
examples.en: Anna: Perfect! That is worth it for everyone.

deeper.text: In a real argument, people mix the three words freely, but they follow a pattern. The first speaker asks Warum? and the answer starts with Weil. The calmer speakers use da to mention what everybody already knows. And denn adds an extra reason without any verb change. Listen for these roles in every discussion, in German or in your own language.

example.de: Weil ich Züge liebe, fahre ich gern mit.
example.en: Because I love trains, I like coming along.

cards.more: Treat the talk as a little play with a script. Ben is the one who asks questions, Mira is the one who answers with weil, Leon and Anna are the calm ones who say da, and Ben adds a final reason with denn. Read it first for the plan: who goes where? Then read it for the words: find every weil, da and denn. Last, play it aloud and swap parts. Three readings, three different jobs.
steps: 1 Read once for the plan: who goes where?
2 Find weil, da and denn: where is the verb in each?
3 Read it aloud with a friend and swap roles.

lessons.title: Können Sie mir sagen, wo …?: getting information about a destination
lessons.goal: Ask a tourist office for information with polite indirect questions, understand the answers (time, price, place, condition) and pass the information on with dass, weil and da.

grammar.topic: Polite indirect questions and passing information on (use)
grammar.point: No new rule: use polite indirect questions (Können Sie mir sagen, wann die Seilbahn fährt? / … ob es eine Gästekarte gibt?) with the verb at the end, and pass the answer on with dass, weil and da (Die Frau hat gesagt, dass die Rundfahrt um 10 Uhr beginnt.).
